registers.label: Spare
lines: The teachers love the long robes and the best seats.
But God sees the widow at the treasury.
The rich gave out of their plenty;
she gave out of her poverty everything she had.
Two small coins, all she owned —
and the jar of meal was not spent.
Come, let us worship the God who lifts the poor.
We bring all that we are. Amen.

registers.label: Immersive
lines: At Zarephath a widow scraped the last handful of meal from the jar, certain it was her final meal — and the jar was not spent; day after day it did not run dry.
She gave out of her poverty all that she had.
At the temple another widow came to the treasury and dropped in two small coins, the least that anyone gave that day.
She gave out of her poverty all that she had.
The rich poured in out of their abundance; she put in everything she owned, her whole living.
She gave out of her poverty all that she had.
This is the God who keeps the jar full and lifts up the poor. Come, bring your whole life and worship.
She gave out of her poverty all that she had. Amen.

registers.label: Hybrid
lines: The widow dropped in two small coins.
We bring all that we have.
She gave not from her plenty but from her need.
We bring all that we have.
At Zarephath the jar of meal was not spent.
We bring all that we have.
Come, let us worship the God who provides.
We bring all that we have. Amen.
